the U.S. Geological Survey estimated undiscovered, technically recoverable mean conventional resources of 7.8 billion barrels of oil and 91.9 trillion cubic feet of gas
The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) assessed the potential for undiscovered, technically recoverable conventional oil and gas resources
The assessment includes an allocation of undiscovered conventional resources within this province to the area north of the Arctic Circle.
has a complex tectonic evolution involving multiple phases of extension, thermal subsidence, movement along regional transform and strike-slip fault systems
as seafloor spreading heralded the opening of the Labrador Sea and Baffin Bay, which were linked by the Ungava transform fault zone.
From the late Eocene to the present, the conjugate margins of eastern Canada and western Greenland have remained passive
Within the TPS, five assessment units (AUs) were redefined from those of 2011 (Schenk, 2011)
The Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland defined the Northwest Greenland Rifted Margin AU, Southwest Greenland Rifted Margin AU
were defined in the compilation of geologic information by Harrison and others (2011) and were also adopted for this assessment
Modeling has indicated that several source rocks have reached the thermal generation windows for oil and gas
Reservoirs related to the first phase of rifting include alluvial fan to fluvial and deltaic channel sandstones
Traps are complex along both margins because several phases of rifting, strike-slip faulting, and contractional deformation have modified original structures.
Regional uplift and erosion related to mantle plumes may have resulted in loss of oil or gas.

notes: USGS Fact Sheet exactly as served (4 pages, US Letter, two columns, tagged). Page 1: USGS banner and logo (not checked: may be an image), series label 'National and Global Petroleum Assessment', the two-line title, a shaded summary box whose first letter is a large italic initial ('U' of 'Using', so the phrase starts after it), 'Introduction' in the left column, the Figure 1 map with its legend in the right column, footers. Page 2: section text in two columns, then Table 1 across the page. Page 3: summary text in two columns, Table 2 across the page, the start of the reference list in two columns. Page 4: references, a shaded box with 'For More Information' and the assessment team, footer. Headings: the first line of the title (the second line, 'of the West Greenland-East Canada Province, 2023', is not part of the listed string), the bold section headings and the two bold headings in the page-4 box; the second box heading is printed 'West Greenland-East Canada Province Assessment Team' and is listed through its last three words to avoid the hyphen, whose code point cannot be seen. Map labels, legend entries and the scale bar are not checked (they may be part of the image). Table 1 is complete and written as the printed 9-column grid: each block repeats the header cell 'Assessment input data—Conventional AUs' (printed over two lines, spanning both header rows; written once in the block's top row with an em dash, U+2014, assumed from its length), the AU name spanning four columns (written in the first), and the Minimum/Median/Maximum/Calculated mean row; the last block fills only five columns. Gray (not applicable) and covered cells are empty strings (not scored). Table 2 is complete: header row 1 has the three row-spanning headers and 'Total undiscovered resources' spanning 12 columns, row 2 the Oil/Gas/NGL groups, row 3 the fractiles; 'AU probability' and 'Accumulation type' are printed hyphenated over three lines ('prob-/ability', 'Accum-/ulation') and written as the words; each AU label and its '1.0' span the Oil and Gas rows and are written in the Oil row; the full-width section rows are written in the first column ('Mesozoic–Cenozoic' with an en dash, U+2013, assumed); total labels are written as the words ('conven-/tional' joined). Every Table 2 column sums to its printed total row, and the summary paragraph's figures (7,769 MMBO; 91,897 BCFG; 5,950 MMBO) match the totals. Noise: no running header or footer repeats (page-1 and page-4 footers differ), so noise is empty. Absent: the body text is ragged-right without one-word hyphenation; two one-word line-end hyphenations occur, 'conven-/tional' in both Table 2 total labels and 'assess-/ment' in the Figure 1 caption, listed in their split forms; compounds broken at a line end ('tectono-/sedimentary', 'Bojesen-/Koefoed') are not listed. BLIND PROTOCOL: chosen and answered before any converter or text extractor was run on the file; every check was typed from the rendered pages (pdftoppm at 90-230 dpi, read as images), and the PDF text layer was never read. Consequences: (1) text that may be an image (logos, mastheads, cover art, chart labels) is not checked; (2) invisible text-layer content cannot be known, so noise lists only VISIBLE repeated page furniture; (3) where the exact code point of a glyph cannot be seen (curly vs straight quotes, dash and minus variants), must_contain phrases and ordered anchors avoid it; headings, table cells and absent entries that cannot avoid it are noted per file.
